coding.description: Architecture, supervision, and delivery; direct work or delegation by judgment

models.guidance: Preferred main coding model via the Subs gateway; second independent pr-reviewer opinion after Opus 5.5 and first tech-lead fallback after Opus 5.5. The configured models do not have overlapping provider routes, so never retry the same model through another provider. Explicit user provider/model selection determines the initial model; fallback remains automatic unless the user explicitly requires that exact model or forbids fallback. On model availability, authentication, or quota failure, inspect any partial work and automatically continue through the configured model chain using a new explicit pi-subagents launch without waiting for confirmation. Report the exact failed model, reason, and fallback model so the transition is observable. Unrelated launch/tooling/workflow failures remain infrastructure blockers under pi-subagents recovery rules. Tech-lead automatic chain: Opus 5.5 (default), then Astra, then public-only Muse; no other fallback, and if none is eligible report the checkpoint as blocked. The PR skill requests independent opinions from both anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 (primary, the pr-reviewer default) and Astra (secondary, explicit per-launch override) on the same patch and criteria when available. Use tech-lead for frontier judgment checkpoints (architecture, difficult tradeoffs, contested decisions) so a cheap main session consults frontier only at high-stakes moments. Reserve for architecture, difficult reasoning, supervision, and final judgment rather than routine implementation. Main-model selection remains independent of identity activation.

Configured default for pr-reviewer, for tech-lead (fallback: Astra, then public-only Muse, nothing else), and for ui-design in either public or private repositories. For ui-design: design direction, interaction specifications, and implementation guidelines, not routine UI implementation. UI implementation belongs to general using the Sol/Grok/GLM/Muse visibility routing and following accepted design guidelines. In the PR skill, Opus is the primary independent opinion and Astra the secondary one, both reviewing the same patch and criteria when available.

Default for implementation (including UI implementation) and explore-codebase in verified public repositories; explicitly select Muse for these launches. For UI implementation, follow accepted design guidelines. Verify the actual repository is public and the handoff contains no private material before using Muse by default; a remote URL alone is not evidence of public visibility. Never send private or unknown-visibility repository context to Muse by default. An explicit user instruction to use Muse overrides this default routing regardless of repository visibility; confirm the requested scope and proceed with the user's choice.

Default for implementation (including UI implementation) in private or unknown-visibility repositories. Also the configured default for general. If Sol is unavailable, authentication fails, or quota is exhausted, inspect any partial work and automatically continue with xai/grok-4.7; if Grok also fails, continue with zai/glm-5.3. Report each failed model and selected fallback. Unrelated launch/tooling/workflow failures remain infrastructure blockers and must not trigger this model fallback chain or an execution-engine change. For UI implementation, follow accepted design guidelines. An explicit user instruction to use another model determines the initial model regardless of repository visibility; fallback remains automatic unless the user explicitly requires that exact route or forbids fallback.

Grok is the first automatic fallback from subs-codex/gpt-6-sol for subagents, including private or unknown-visibility repository work. If Grok is unavailable, authentication fails, or quota is exhausted, continue with zai/glm-5.3 as the final fallback. Inspect any partial work before switching models, report the failed model and selected fallback, and do not retry through another provider route. Explicit user provider/model selection determines the initial model; fallback remains automatic unless the user explicitly requires that exact route or forbids fallback.

Final automatic fallback for implementation (including UI implementation) in private or unknown-visibility repositories and for general, after subs-codex/gpt-6-sol and xai/grok-4.7. Inspect any partial work before switching, report the failed model and selected fallback, and do not retry GLM, Sol, or Grok through another provider. Unrelated launch/tooling/workflow failures remain infrastructure blockers and must not trigger this fallback or an execution-engine change. For UI implementation, follow accepted design guidelines. An explicit user instruction to use another model determines the initial model regardless of repository visibility; fallback remains automatic unless the user explicitly requires that exact route or forbids fallback.

Configured default for explore-codebase in private or unknown-visibility repositories, and for web-researcher regardless of repository visibility. For explore-codebase in verified public repositories, explicitly select Muse instead. An explicit user instruction to use Muse overrides visibility routing.
